import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 839

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/839](https://www.erdosproblems.com/839)
- [Er78f] Erdős, P., *Problems in number theory and combinatorics*, Proc. Sixth Manitoba Conf. on
  Numerical Math. (1978), 35-58.
- [Er92c] Erdős, P., *Some of my favourite unsolved problems*, J. Combin. Theory Ser. A (1992).

See also [Erdős Problem 359](https://www.erdosproblems.com/359) and
[Erdős Problem 867](https://www.erdosproblems.com/867).
-/

open Filter Real Finset
open scoped ENNReal

namespace Erdos839

/-- A sequence $a : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ is "sum-of-consecutive-free" if no term equals
the sum of a contiguous block of earlier terms. That is, for all $i$,
$a_i \neq a_j + a_{j+1} + \cdots + a_k$ for any $j \leq k < i$. -/
def SumOfConsecutiveFree (a : ℕ → ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ i : ℕ, ∀ j k : ℕ, j ≤ k → k < i →
    a i ≠ ∑ l ∈ Finset.Icc j k, a l

/--
Erdős Problem 839 (Part 1) [Er78f][Er92c]:

Let $1 \leq a_1 < a_2 < \cdots$ be a strictly increasing sequence of positive integers
such that no $a_i$ is the sum of consecutive $a_j$ for $j < i$.
Is it true that $\limsup a_n / n = \infty$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_839.parts.i : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (a : ℕ → ℕ), (∀ n, 1 ≤ a n) → StrictMono a → SumOfConsecutiveFree a →
    atTop.limsup (fun n : ℕ => (a n : ℝ≥0∞) / n) = ⊤ := by
  sorry

/--
Erdős Problem 839 (Part 2, stronger) [Er78f][Er92c]:

Let $1 \leq a_1 < a_2 < \cdots$ be a strictly increasing sequence of positive integers
such that no $a_i$ is the sum of consecutive $a_j$ for $j < i$.
Is it true that $\lim_{x \to \infty} \frac{1}{\log x} \sum_{a_n < x} \frac{1}{a_n} = 0$?

This is equivalent to asking whether the range $\{a_1,a_2,\ldots\}$ has logarithmic density zero
(see `Set.HasLogDensity`).
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_839.parts.ii : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (a : ℕ → ℕ), (∀ n, 1 ≤ a n) → StrictMono a → SumOfConsecutiveFree a →
    Set.HasLogDensity (Set.range a) 0 := by
  sorry

-- TODO: Formalize the additional material on the possible lower limit, reciprocal-sum growth,
-- upper-density constructions, and the links with Erdős Problems 359 and 867.

end Erdos839

findings.description: The module bibliography identifies [Er92c] as “Some of my favourite unsolved problems”, J. Combin. Theory Ser. A (1992). The relevant 1992 source is instead “Some of my forgotten problems in number theory”, Hardy–Ramanujan Journal 15 (1992), 34–50. Both formalized questions occur on page 42, following equation (19). This is a bibliographic error; the mathematical statements are faithful.
findings.source_evidence: The publisher’s record at https://hrj.episciences.org/125 gives the title “Some of my forgotten problems in number theory” and volume 15 (1992). The PDF, https://hrj.episciences.org/125/pdf, p. 42, asks whether the consecutive-sum condition forces lower density zero, and then whether it forces logarithmic density zero.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the [Er92c] entry with: Erdős, P., Some of my forgotten problems in number theory. Hardy–Ramanujan J. 15 (1992), 34–50, especially pp. 42–43. Link to https://hrj.episciences.org/125.

reformulations.difference: The 1992 primary paper asks whether the sequence has lower density zero. Lean uses an infinite ENNReal limsup of a n / n, with a zero-based sequence.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For a strictly increasing positive enumeration b₁,b₂,…, the lower density of its range equals liminf n/bₙ. This is zero exactly when limsup bₙ/n is infinite. Relabeling bₙ₊₁ = a n preserves the sequence hypotheses. For n ≥ 1, a n/(n+1) ≤ a n/n ≤ 2·a n/(n+1), so the infinite-limsup condition is unchanged. Although the n=0 ENNReal quotient is infinite, a limsup ignores a finite prefix. The denominator-shift equivalence and finite-prefix behavior were proved in Lean; the full lower-density characterization was checked mathematically.

reformulations.difference: Lean expresses the source’s normalized reciprocal-sum limit using Set.HasLogDensity on Set.range a. That definition uses integer cutoffs k ≤ N, whereas the source writes aₙ < x.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: StrictMono makes a injective, so summing over range values counts every sequence term exactly once. Positivity excludes the zero reciprocal. For N ≥ 2, changing ≤ N to < N changes the normalized sum by at most 1/(N log N), which tends to zero; this cutoff equivalence was proved in Lean. Integer and real cutoffs are also equivalent: for N = floor x ≥ 2, the nonnegative normalized sum below x is bounded above by the sum through N divided by log N. Conversely, a real-variable limit restricts to integer cutoffs. The exceptional logarithms at 0 and 1 affect only a finite prefix. The full real-cutoff equivalence was checked mathematically, not proved in Lean.

review.notes: No mathematical misformalization was found in the definition or either theorem. Scratch files scratch.lean, reindex.lean, and logdensity.lean under /workspace/review compile successfully. They check the boundary cases, establish powers of two as a positive strictly increasing admissible sequence, and prove the indexing and cutoff equivalences without sorry. The live erdosproblems.com pages and bibliography returned HTTP 403 despite descriptive User-Agent headers. Thus their latest remarks/status and the exact [Er78f] bibliography-key mapping could not be independently checked. The primary 1992 paper verifies both mathematical claims; the current community database lists Problem 839 as open.
